title: Riverview Bank - Data Residency & Compliance Discovery
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment
summary: Initial discovery with Riverview Bank to understand residency requirements (EU/US), logging restrictions for customer PII, and whether Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private fits their compliance constraints. Customer prefers Dedicated or Private due to audit and KMS needs but is open to a limited-hosted pilot with strict logging controls and EU-only routing.
next_steps: Sofia to send SOC2 report, GDPR Data Processing Addendum (DPA), and HIPAA guidance (by 2026-03-06)
Liam to propose benchmark plan for latency/cost (by 2026-03-10)
Customer to confirm legal review timeline and internal stakeholders for pilot (by 2026-03-09)
Schedule technical POC kick-off (tentative week of 2026-03-16)

Liam - Draft POC benchmark plan and model/sequence profile questions - due 2026-03-10

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Karen Liu (Riverview CISO), Tom Becker (Riverview CTO), Aisha Rahman (Riverview Compliance)

Auto-summary: Discussed residency needs for EU and US, logging restrictions and PII handling, tradeoffs between Hosted/Dedicated/Private, and next steps to send security docs and scope a POC.

00:00:05 - Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time, i'm Sofia from Redwood, this is Liam, our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
00:00:13 - Karen: Good, thanks. busy week but good to be here.
00:00:20 - Tom: Yep, thanks. want to get into the residency requirements.
00:00:28 - Sofia: Perfect. quick agenda: we want to understand your compliance constraints, current infra, what success looks like, and then talk through hosted vs dedicated vs private. and obviously answer any security questions. sound ok?
00:00:40 - Aisha: yep sounds good.
00:00:45 - Liam: i'll probably ask some perf and architecture questions as we go — mostly around token volumes, latency tolerances, and whether KV cache or prefix caching needs to persist across requests.
00:00:56 - Karen: quick context: Riverview's customer data includes account numbers, names, some SSNs historically, we limit SSN storage but transcripts and chat logs can contain PII. we have EU-based customers and regulators want EU data residency for those accounts.
00:01:15 - Sofia: Understood. do you currently have any model infra? are you calling external APIs today?
00:01:22 - Tom: We have some internal LLM experiments, but most prod calls hit third-party APIs in the US. legal's flagged that for EU customers we need data residency and stronger audit capability.
00:01:35 - Sofia: Got it. so high-level we typically see three paths: Hosted (Redwood API) with region-specific routing and DPAs, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools for your org), or Private (VPC / on-prem where control plane sits in your environment). each has different tradeoffs for control, latency, and operational burden.
00:01:53 - Karen: our main ask — can we guarantee EU-only storage and logs for EU customer traffic, and also limit logs that contain PII or redact them?
00:02:03 - Liam: yes, we support region-based routing so EU requests can stay within EU regions. for Hosted we can enable EU-only routing and retention controls, but some customers prefer Dedicated or Private because they want customer-managed KMS and no Redwood access to raw logs.
00:02:20 - Aisha: what about audit logs and retention? regulators want full audit trails but with PII redaction in logs after a short window. is that doable?
00:02:30 - Sofia: we can provide detailed request/response audit logs for a limited retention period; we also offer redaction and tokenization tooling. for Dedicated we can configure longer or shorter retention and give you control over exporting logs to your SIEM. for Private you control the entire lifecycle.
00:02:46 - Tom: curious about encryption at rest and KMS integration — we need CMK/HSM integration, preferably customer-managed keys.
00:02:55 - Liam: Dedicated supports customer KMS integration (Cloud KMS, HSM) and Private supports on-prem HSM. Hosted can support bring-your-own-key in some regions — there's typically a legal and security review but it's possible.
00:03:12 - Karen: ok. next — logging restrictions: we need to make sure transcripts and model logs aren't retained longer than X days and that sensitive fields are redacted at ingestion. does Redwood offer field-level redaction?
00:03:23 - Liam: yes we have a pre-processing filter you can run client-side, or we can wire it into the ingest pipeline to redact known sensitive patterns (SSNs, account numbers). note transcription may not be perfect — sometimes numbers get merged — so we recommend deterministic token-level filters plus manual review for edge cases.
00:03:42 - Aisha: HIPAA — while we are not a healthcare provider, some of our partners are and we want to ensure the platform can meet HIPAA controls when necessary. is Redwood HIPAA-capable?
00:03:52 - Sofia: Redwood supports HIPAA through Private deployments and in some Dedicated configurations with BAA. For Hosted, we have customers on HIPAA workloads but they typically require a dedicated, compliant enclave and contract-level BAA.
00:04:07 - Tom: about model caching — does Redwood persist KV cache or prefixes in a way that could leak PII between requests?
00:04:17 - Liam: good question. the runtime isolates KV caches per customer and per model instance. for Hosted we do ephemeral caching and can disable persistent caches; for Dedicated we give you more control and for Private you can manage cache entirely. we also have policies to scrub cached state when it contains PII. there are tradeoffs — disabling cache can increase latency/cost.
00:04:38 - Karen: tradeoffs is what we care about. we need sub-200ms median latency for certain flows, and also cost predictability. how do you recommend balancing that?
00:04:49 - Liam: typically we recommend Dedicated with tuned batching and caching for production SLAs. Hosted can meet latency if routed to closest region and with optimized models, but Dedicated gives you the reserved capacity so tail latency is more predictable. Private is best for full control but adds ops overhead.
00:05:08 - Sofia: i'll note that for EU residency + customer KMS + strict log controls, customers often choose Dedicated first to get the operational SLA and then move to Private if they need full on-prem.
00:05:18 - Tom: what about governance and RBAC? we need strict role separation and SSO integration (SAML/SCIM) and audit trails for actions.
00:05:27 - Liam: we support SSO via SAML, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC with fine-grained roles. audit trails track config changes, access, and API keys. for Dedicated/Private you can integrate logs into your SIEM, and for Hosted we provide tenant-level audit logs.
00:05:43 - Aisha: any regulatory certifications — SOC2, ISO?
00:05:47 - Sofia: Redwood has SOC2 Type II and is pursuing ISO 27001 — we'll include the SOC2 report in the security package. HIPAA is supported via BAA for Dedicated/Private as mentioned.
00:05:58 - Karen: legal's also worried about cross-border transfers — if we have EU customers, we need assurances that PII will not be processed outside the EU. how strict is your region routing?
00:06:09 - Liam: we can pin routing by account and by request. for Hosted, EU-only routing is standard for EU-flagged tenants; we also support IP-based and geo headers. Dedicated gives you physical capacity in EU regions; Private keeps everything inside your VPC.
00:06:24 - Tom: ok. let's talk about pilot scope — we want to run a small pilot with a handful of EU customer flows, measure latency, token cost, and ensure logs are redacted. can Redwood do a short benchmark?
00:06:36 - Sofia: absolutely. we usually propose a 2-4 week POC: initial data residency and security review, a small benchmark with representative sequences, and then a longer pilot if results are good.
00:06:47 - Karen: what data do you need from us to run the benchmark?
00:06:51 - Liam: primarily sample prompt/response pairs or length distributions, token volumes per minute, and expected concurrency. also tell us the models you want to evaluate (open models vs curated). we'll simulate production load and measure median and p95 latency and cost per 1k tokens.
00:07:06 - Tom: we prefer open models with quantization to reduce cost but need to ensure quality for financial language.
00:07:12 - Liam: that's common. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and batching settings. for Dedicated we can pin quantized model builds that meet your perf and quality thresholds.
00:07:22 - Aisha: on logging retention — auditors require 90 days of unredacted audit logs for certain investigations, but we want PII to be redacted after 14 days. can that split exist?
00:07:34 - Sofia: yes, you can keep metadata and operational logs for 90 days, while redacted versions of content can live longer; the raw PII content can be truncated after your retention window. for Dedicated we can implement those policies and have logs exported to your SIEM for long-term retention.
00:07:53 - Karen: is there any chance Redwood employees see raw customer data in Hosted?
00:07:58 - Liam: by default no — access is audited and controlled. for Hosted there are internal access policies and we can limit support access to metadata unless required for debugging; for Dedicated/Private you can restrict access further. we also offer support workflows where you can provide sanitized reproductions for debugging.
00:08:14 - Tom: network connectivity — for Private we'd want a direct connect or VPN to keep traffic off the public internet. supported?
00:08:20 - Liam: yes, Private supports VPN/direct connect and VPC peering. Dedicated can also be placed in a customer VPC in some cloud regions to restrict egress.
00:08:29 - Sofia: quick clarification on PII in model fine-tuning: you mentioned you have some historical data. we recommend not uploading raw PII for fine-tuning unless it's fully anonymized and agreed in the contract.
00:08:41 - Aisha: understood, we'll avoid that.
00:08:44 - Karen: any third-party subprocessors we should be aware of?
00:08:48 - Sofia: we list cloud providers and a small set of telemetry processors; we'll include subprocessors in the DPA. you can also request more restrictive subprocessors via enterprise contracts.
00:08:58 - Tom: pricing — high level, what are the delta's between Hosted and Dedicated costs?
00:09:04 - Sofia: Hosted is usage-based and typically lower upfront, Dedicated has an annual/monthly reserved capacity fee plus usage for overages. Dedicated gives you cost predictability at scale. We'll send a formal pricing sheet after this call.
00:09:17 - Karen: perfect. two other quick technical items: 1) can we ingest logs directly into Splunk? 2) can we configure automatic PII redaction regexes?
00:09:27 - Liam: 1) yes, we have sinks for Splunk/Datadog/SIEM. 2) yes, you can configure regex-based redaction and we can suggest patterns for financial fields.
00:09:38 - Aisha: do you have any references in financial services with similar residency and KMS needs?
00:09:44 - Sofia: yes — we have a couple of mid-market banks and a payments provider who run Dedicated with customer KMS and EU routing. i'll share redacted case studies and references in the security package.
00:09:57 - Tom: great. any blockers from our side to start a pilot?
00:10:02 - Aisha: legal needs to review DPA and SOC2; compliance needs the redaction proof-of-concept; operations needs short timing on network setup.
00:10:12 - Sofia: makes sense. we'll get the SOC2 and DPA over, and Liam will draft the benchmark. if legal signs the DPA quickly we can start the hosted EU-only pilot while Dedicated capacity is provisioned.
00:10:25 - Karen: would Redwood support a canary approach? we want to start with non-sensitive flows first.
00:10:30 - Liam: absolutely — start with low-sensitivity EU flows, validate redaction and routing, then expand.
00:10:36 - Sofia: ok let's capture next steps.
00:10:40 - Liam: i'll follow up with the benchmark template and questions about token distributions.
00:10:44 - Sofia: i'll send SOC2, DPA, subprocessors, HIPAA guidance, and redacted references.
00:10:51 - Aisha: i'll send our compliance checklist and retention policy.
00:10:55 - Karen: we'll aim to get legal review timeboxed to two weeks.
00:11:00 - Sofia: perfect. any other questions?
00:11:03 - Tom: not from me.
00:11:05 - Aisha: none.
00:11:07 - Sofia: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the package and a proposed POC plan.
00:11:12 - Karen: thanks, bye.
00:11:15 - Sofia: bye.
